message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a purchase: total net sales of $391.0B (up 2% from $383.3B), operating income of $123.2B, net income of $93.7B, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3B — with gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% on strong Services growth (+13% to $96.2B, 73.9% services gross margin) and $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. Net income dipped slightly year over year only because of a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not an operating deterioration; the company also returned $95.0B via buybacks and $15.2B in dividends. Risks I weighed include the 8% Greater China sales decline, DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure, and supply-chain concentration. I placed one buy order for 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.70, essentially the current quote (last $222.70, bid $222.68/ask $222.72), for about $9,799 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, the $20,000 daily cap, and the buy-only, AAPL/MSFT-only mandate, with no money moved out of the account (cash was $50,000 and the only existing position is 100 MSFT shares). Note: my first submission was rejected by the order gate because I had rounded revenue to $395.0B; I resubmitted using the exact reported figures and the order filled at $222.70.
